newsitem.title: USA: US debt allocations little changed Oct 8 wk-survey.
newsitem.headline: US debt allocations little changed Oct 8 wk-survey.

text.p: A mixed employment report last week clouded U.S. money managers' outlook on debt allocations, according to a survey by Stone & McCarthy Research Associates Inc.
"The data suggest that the September employment release had varied effects on money manager perceptions of the appropriate portfolio structure," the report said.
"Neither duration exposure nor cash holdings changed to any significant degree," the report added.

In the week ended October 8, the survey's bear/bull index arithmetic reading fell to 4.16 from 4.36 the previous week, while the asset-weighted number slumped to 4.03, down from 4.39 in the previous period, according the report.
A number above 5.00 is seen as indicating investors are mostly long on the market.
The cash/assets ratio rose to 7.08 percent from 7.06 percent.
Duration bogey held mostly steady at 4.06 on an arithmetic basis and 4.68 on a weighted basis.
Duration bogey is the level of asset or liability duration sought in the management of a portfolio.
Duration refers to a portfolio's average maturity and is used by portfolio managers to calculate exposure to risk.

Twenty-four percent of the portfolio managers polled said they were planning to be active in the coming week, up sharply from 4 percent the week before. The bear/bull index collected among those intending to be active was 4.17, down from 5.0 the previous week.
The Stone & McCarthy survey is conducted by the research firm weekly. It includes 25 market participants with total assets of about $100 billion, the firm said.
* Table provided by Stone and McCarthy Research Associates.
** Respondents intending to adjust portfolio in coming week.
